thesis: The rasikhun close their du'a by naming two certainties instead of a request — Allah is the Gatherer and the mi'ad cannot be missed — with the petition elided (Tabari's hadhf) and the final clause possibly God's own speech (Jalalayn's iltifat reading), so the one fixed certainty of the Day lets the rooted heart hold every other ambiguity open.

flags.quote: the classical commentators have a startling suggestion about who finishes the line
flags.issue: Plural overstates: only al-Jalalayn carries the God's-own-speech possibility; body text later attributes correctly to him alone.

notes: Every countable claim verified exactly (10 masc at listed refs; 4 fem all sa'a; jam' 6/6 Day-verses, 0/4 others; 3:25 word-for-word 16 ayahs later). All attributions verbatim (Tabari hadhf + mif'al note; Jalalayn maw'id bi-l-ba'th; Muyassar nuqirru wa-nashhad). Rasikhun attribution of the du'a explicitly in Tabari + Ibn Kathir. Independently cross-checked by lead reviewer in-session — counts match. Minor flag does not affect verdict.

thesis: Once ownership of everything is settled as Allah's alone, the certain gathering arrives wrapped in the mercy He has written upon Himself, so accountability becomes bearable and the real catastrophe is losing one's own self.
notes: Makes NO rarity claim about kataba 'ala nafsihi (occurs 6:12 AND 6:54 — a uniqueness claim would have failed; none present). Emphatic la-yajma'annakum confirmed. Mercy-as-invitation carried by Tabari + Jalalayn + Ibn Kathir's rahmati-taghlibu hadith. Not ahkam-bearing.
